about.title: Marina Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Marina's mix of light industrial sites, agricultural operations, and commercial corridors along Reservation Road and Del Monte Boulevard means workplace injuries here often involve more than one responsible party. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation regardless of fault, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured workers in Marina with an independent attorney who can look at the full picture, including whether a third-party claim applies alongside any comp benefits you're pursuing. Given Monterey County's blend of employers and job sites, it helps to have someone sort out where your case actually fits.

whyChoose.title: Why Marina Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Look Past the Comp System
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the usual exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be held separately liable. An attorney can help determine if that applies to your situation.

items.title: We Understand the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California law requires injuries to be reported to an employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp eligibility. Missing that window can complicate your case, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: We Respect the Two-Year Clock on Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Separate injury claims against a negligent third party generally follow California's two-year statute of limitations. An attorney can help make sure that deadline isn't missed while your comp claim is still being sorted out.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Imjin Parkway — can I still file a claim if my employer says it's just workers' comp?
items.answer: Workers' comp usually is the exclusive remedy against your employer, but that doesn't rule out a separate claim against a third party who contributed to the accident, like a subcontractor or equipment supplier. An independent attorney can review the details of your job site injury to see if that applies. LawProactive can connect you with someone free of charge to sort through it.

items.question: What if I was injured while driving for work somewhere along Reservation Road or Del Monte Boulevard?
items.answer: If another driver caused the crash while you were performing work duties, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a separate injury claim against that driver. These situations often involve more moving parts than a typical on-site injury. An attorney can help determine how the two claims interact.

items.question: Can my employer retaliate against me for reporting a workplace injury in Marina?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, that's worth raising with an attorney right away. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles these concerns alongside your injury claim.
